title: Certificate Servicing Note: Standing Instructions Recorded Against a Certificate of Deposit
content:
Three instructions stand against a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line: what is to happen at maturity, where credited interest is to go, and which Piedmont Crescent account is to receive money paid out.

## 1. When a change may be recorded

The owner may change the renewal instruction, the interest disposition or the payout account at any time while the certificate is active or in its grace period.

## 2. The renewal instruction and the maturity it governs

A change to the renewal instruction must be recorded before the grace period ends if it is to govern the maturity now at hand. A change recorded after that governs the next maturity instead.

| When the change is recorded | Maturity it governs |
|---|---|
| while the certificate is active, before maturity | the maturity now at hand |
| during the grace period, before it ends | the maturity now at hand |
| after the grace period has ended | the next maturity |

## 3. The interest disposition

A disposition must be one of the dispositions the tier lists, and it takes effect from the next crediting date. Interest already credited under the previous disposition is not redirected.

## 4. The payout account

The payout account must be a checking or a savings account of the same customer, in active status at the moment the instruction is recorded. An instruction to pay interest or proceeds out that names no such account is not accepted.

The account's ownership and status are read from the bank's own records for that account, not from the customer's account of them. An account belonging to a spouse, or one of the customer's own accounts that is closed or otherwise not active, does not satisfy the condition.

## 5. A reading of the three together

An owner of a 12-Month Certificate whose interest is compounding asks in the eighth month for it to be paid to their checking account instead. That disposition is among the three the tier lists, the checking account is theirs and active, and so the instruction is recorded; it governs the crediting at the end of that month onward, and the interest compounded in the first seven months stays in the certificate.
